Focus segment: Premium Thin & Light. Premium Thin & Light has the highest recent battery complaint rate (6.9% [6.7%, 7.1%], E001). It is also the only segment with a material rise: 4.4% to 6.9%, diff +2.5% (CI +2.2% to +2.8%), q_value_bh 0.0, status intensified_long_standing (E005). So the issue is long-standing and has intensified, not new. Budget rose by only +0.3% and was labelled no_material_change even though q=0.014 (E002). Gaming (E003) and Mainstream (E004) show no significant change. Complaints are spread across 28 products, and the top product accounts for 12.6% of recent complaints (E005), so the signal is not driven by one product. These are descriptive complaint rates only. They contain no distribution or consumer-preference measures, and they cannot show cause.
Declared H1 (complaint_comparison, two-sided): Premium Thin & Light products positioned on battery life have a different post-first-sale battery complaint rate than their segment cohort.

Declared H2 (complaint_comparison, less): Premium Thin & Light products positioned on battery life have lower post-first-sale battery complaint rates than non-positioned cohort products. This would be an association only, not evidence that the product solved the need.
Declared H3 (launch_trajectory, two-sided): Premium Thin & Light products positioned on battery life show different sales per active model after their estimated first observed sale than the cohort.

P0113: positioned_on_need. Battery endurance is the headline selling point. Estimated first observed sale is 2023-M10 and usable (E009). Cohort has 15 models (E012). I removed P0050 from the comparison set because it is also positioned on battery. No price-and-volume pattern (E014). Mean segment share over the first 12 months

P0050: positioned_on_need. All-day battery is a lead claim, so I judged this positioned. Estimated first observed sale is 2023-M11 and usable (E010). Cohort has 15 models (E013). An observed price-and-volume pattern appears in 2024-M02 and 2024-M03; no promotion records exist, so none can be confirmed (E015). Share was 5.66%

P0120: positioned_on_need. Battery life is one of two headline claims, so this is weak or borderline positioning. Its first observed sale is unreliable (coverage_expansion_month, no_visible_ramp, and the document precedes first sale by 7 months) (E011). I did not run launch or cohort comparisons for it.

Alternative for P0113: Cohort-composition artefact: the cohort was matched only on first-sale month and early ASP. It includes P0050, which is also battery-positioned, and unlabeled products. P0113's 18.09% share may reflect factors the matching ignores, such as brand, form factor, display, or channel. The data hold no distribution or availability measures. The note that P0113's first-month units were 5,860 and its early peak 21,541 (E009) suggests an unusually large launch scale.

Alternative for P0113: Complaint-pool dilution: a large buyer base (share 18%) could mean a different buyer mix, with more casual users who complain less. Comment volume may also scale differently. P0113 has 4,826 comments versus 1,465 for P0050, so the rate may reflect who comments, not battery performance. Comment propensity could differ by product.

Alternative for P0113: Timing and first-sale artefact: 'first 12 months' is anchored on an estimated first observed sale. A panel-coverage change could shift the window. Share is also relative to the segment total in those months. Segment composition, and entries or exits by competitors, could change P0113's share without any change in the product.

Alternative for P0050: Small-sample and low-power issue: the null results (q=0.47, 0.64, 0.54) do not show that the product matched its cohort. Wide cohort variance (complaint rates 4.3% to 14.1%) and n=14 limit power. P0050 has only 1,465 comments. Its price-and-volume months reduce the usable window to 10 months. An absence of difference is not evidence of equivalence.

Alternative for P0050: Price effects: the ASP drop of up to 22.9% with a unit rise in 2024-M02 and 2024-M03 could affect both share and the buyer mix, which may include more price-sensitive buyers. Excluding those months did not change the outcome, but price differences within the cohort (30% tolerance) remain uncontrolled.

Alternative for P0113: Segment-level battery complaint rise (E005) concerns 2024-M07 onward, while the product comparisons use 2023-M10 to 2024-M10 windows. The windows only partially overlap, so the product-level results cannot speak to the segment rise. Product-level explanations such as firmware updates or battery hardware are also not tested.
